correctness.rationale: For N>=5 and t in [1/2,1] the four short cycle distances define a metric (only 1<=2t is critical). Vertices of the dual Lipschitz polytope are exactly potentials with connected tight-edge graphs by active incidence rank. The outside range-one vs range-less-than-one dichotomy forces binary outside values and a core anchored at 0 or 1; tight walks give precisely four possible core values 0,1-t,t,1 (three at t=1/2). Independent enumeration of ALL 4^4 core tuples and tight components at rational t=1/2,2/3,3/4,7/8 confirms (A,B)=(26,15) at the boundary and (38,27) in the open interval. Combining A(2^k-2)+2B for k=N-4 gives 26*2^k-22 and 38*2^k-22; at equilateral t=1, all nonconstant binary potentials give 2^N-2. Checks are finite corroboration; the anchored-value and rank proofs establish arbitrary N and all real t.
